list.query: SELECT initcap(COALESCE(NULLIF(r.category, 'unknown'), 'other')) || ' · ' || COALESCE(r.display_name, m.metric) || COALESCE(' (' || NULLIF(r.unit_canonical, '') || ')', '') AS __text, m.metric AS __value FROM (SELECT DISTINCT metric FROM daily_metrics WHERE day > current_date - 180) m LEFT JOIN metric_registry r USING (metric) ORDER BY COALESCE(NULLIF(r.category, 'unknown'), 'zz'), 1

options.content:
Every measure your devices sent in the last six months, one chart each, grouped by kind. Nothing to choose: a measure your watch doesn't record simply isn't listed, and older watches report fewer.

The bars are each day's value: a total for things that add up (steps, exercise minutes, energy), an average for things that are measured (heart rate, walking speed), the lowest reading for resting heart rate. The dashed line is the 7-day average, which shows the trend under the day-to-day noise.

Heart rate variability (HRV) is how much the time between heartbeats varies; it runs higher when you're rested and is very personal, so compare it with your own history, not other people's. Resting heart rate is the lowest steady rate of the day. Walking asymmetry and double support come from the iPhone in your pocket: how evenly you step, and how much of each stride both feet are on the ground.

panels.title: $metric
panels.description: Each day's value (bars) and the 7-day average (dashed).

targets.rawSql:
SELECT (day::timestamp AT TIME ZONE '$tz') AS time,
  CASE COALESCE(r.agg_default, 'avg') WHEN 'sum' THEN d.sum WHEN 'min' THEN d.vmin WHEN 'max' THEN d.vmax ELSE d.avg END
    AS "Daily",
  AVG(CASE COALESCE(r.agg_default, 'avg') WHEN 'sum' THEN d.sum WHEN 'min' THEN d.vmin WHEN 'max' THEN d.vmax
      ELSE d.avg END) OVER (ORDER BY d.day ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS "7-day average"
FROM daily_metrics d LEFT JOIN metric_registry r USING (metric)
WHERE d.metric = '$metric' AND $__timeFilter((day::timestamp AT TIME ZONE '$tz'))
ORDER BY d.day
